items.title: OpenAI is stepping back from NDAs for data center projects

items.content:
The ChatGPT maker won’t use NDAs with public officials as part of its new data center community commitments.

Following this week’s midterms where voters resoundingly voiced their opposition to data center expansion , OpenAI today announced new commitments to communities where it is working on data center projects, including that it won’t use non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) with public officials.

Many data center projects have come under scrutiny for relying on NDAs to hide discussions between developers and local officials. However, OpenAI says it is now allowing “only narrow protections covering legitimate security information, trade secrets, or proprietary or competitively sensitive information.” In October, Amazon announced it would no longer use NDAs with government agencies it works with on data center projects.

OpenAI’s additional commitments include paying “the full cost” of electricity it uses and the “infrastructure needed to serve us.” It will make opportunities for local communities by publishing the jobs it expects to create and by reporting on hiring. And every future “compute campus” (its rebranding phrase for data centers ) the company owns and operates will have a “local compact” that includes the commitments and will reflect “local priorities,” OpenAI says.

items.title: Airbnb is working on an AI travel agent
items.summary: Airbnb plans to roll out an AI agent in the first half of 2027 that will help users plan and book travel, the company said in its Q3 2026 earnings shareholder letter released today. "Today's AI agents are good at simple, routine tasks, like making a restaurant reservation or sche
items.content:
The travel company is planning an “AI-native” trip-planning experience that’s set to roll out next year.

Airbnb plans to roll out an AI agent in the first half of 2027 that will help users plan and book travel, the company said in its Q3 2026 earnings shareholder letter released today .

“Today’s AI agents are good at simple, routine tasks, like making a restaurant reservation or scheduling an appointment,” Airbnb said. “But planning a trip on Airbnb is different.” The company argued that its experience matching hosts and guests, its current role in being part of reservations already, and a “new interface” built “specifically for travel” gives it an edge.

Here’s how Airbnb says that new interface will work:

We don’t think a traditional chatbot is the right way to plan a trip. We’re developing a custom-designed, AI-native experience that builds the interface around your question. Rather than a chat window, our agent draws on a library of hundreds of travel-specific interface elements—maps, photos, comparisons, calendars, itineraries—and composes them in real time to match what you’re looking for. Our agent will help guests explore options, make decisions with the people they’re traveling with, and take action directly in Airbnb.

Airbnb co-founder and CEO Brian Chesky has said before that the company plans to launch an agent in 2027, telling the Skift Global Forum that it would have an interface that’s “much richer than a chatbot.”

In its shareholder letter, Airbnb also said that AI is “the best thing to ever happen to Airbnb” and has changed how it develops products and operates.

items.title: Meta, Google, and TikTok sue California AG over teen social media law
items.summary: If it goes into effect next year, this California law would restrict social media access for children under 16.
items.content:
Meta, Google, and TikTok have each filed lawsuits against California Attorney General Rob Bonta in an attempt to block a law that restricts social media features it deems addictive for users under 16.

California Governor Gavin Newsom signed the bill, known as AB 1709 , into law in September, and it’s slated to take effect at the start of the new year.

The law prohibits social platforms from offering autoplay videos and personalized feeds to users under 16, and it requires the platforms to delete these users’ accounts if they don’t turn those features off. If platforms do not comply, they could be liable for fines of up to $50,000 per affected user under 16 years old.

Meta claims that AB 1709 violates the First Amendment by overriding its editorial decisions about how to display content, adding that Section 230 preempts the law. TikTok and Google made similar arguments.

“Meta currently organizes its feeds of content to include personalized content recommendations and to automatically play media, [so] the Act would make it unlawful for Meta to disseminate speech to minors altogether, and would require Meta to delete minors’ accounts, unless it changes these practices,” the company wrote in its lawsuit.

In an emailed statement, a TikTok spokesperson added, “AB 1709 is a blatantly unconstitutional restriction on free expression that erodes the long-standing and protected practice of curating content based on user preferences, which book stores, TV networks and streaming services all use.”

AB 1709 follows a trend of legislation around the world that seeks to curb teen social media use in an attempt to improve teen mental health outcomes. However, digital safety experts often caution against these laws because they can inadvertently compromise the privacy of all platform users, including adults, by requiring age verification checks that collect more user data.

“AB 1709 compels platforms to collect even more information from every user, invading everyone’s privacy and frustrating our ability to remain anonymous online,” EFF Associate Director of State Affairs Rindala Alajaji said in a press briefing. “Online surveillance by social media companies is harmful, and yet this bill requires even more of it, further concentrating power in the hands of tech companies rather than actually protecting users.”

Alajaji added that teenagers’ use of social media has been instrumental in enabling impactful digital activism, citing the Parkland shooting survivors’ March for Our Lives and climate activist Greta Thunberg’s global reach.

“As a functional ban on social media for youth under 16, AB 1709 cuts young people off from essential information and experiences, silencing the very voices it claims to protect,” Alajaji said.

These platforms are primed to fight this California law as they navigate similar legal battles in various countries. That’s especially true for Meta, which agreed to pay a settlement of up to $18 billion to resolve children’s safety claims brought by 29 U.S. states.

In December 2025, Australia became the first country to ban social media for users under 16 altogether. France passed a similar law, but its top court struck it down , citing concerns about violations of free expression rights.

These platforms also argue that the law would affect parents’ ability to make decisions about their teens’ internet use through parental controls.

A Google spokesperson noted that autoplay on YouTube is turned off for minors by default, and that parents have the ability to turn off their teens’ access to Shorts altogether.

“We believe parents are best positioned to make the right decisions for their families, which is why we offer a range of protections and tools that put parents in control,” a Google spokesperson said. “Overly broad laws like this actually break the systems we’ve built to help kids find high-quality, age-appropriate videos.”

A representative for Attorney General Bonta said that his office is reviewing the filings and is committed to “defending California’s commonsense laws to protect kids online.”

items.content:
저자들은 대기업에서 AI를 도입한 후 실패를 거쳐 35,000명의 실사용자를 확보하기까지의 판단 과정과 전략을 공유합니다. 이 책은 단순한 성공 사례가 아닌 실패와 극복의 기록을 통해 AI 도입을 고민하는 조직이 시행착오를 줄일 수 있도록 돕습니다.

연말이 다가오면 기업마다 내년 사업계획과 예산을 짠다. 올해는 그 서류 맨 앞에 AI 전환(AX)이 올라온 곳이 많다. 영풍문고 북마스터가 이번 주 고른 『실전 AX 리포트』는 이 시기에 계획서를 쓰는 사람이 먼저 읽어 볼 만한 기록이다. 한빛미디어가 지난 8월 30일 펴냈다.

책은 한 대기업 AX 팀이 1개 부서에서 시작해 52개 계열사, 3만5000명에게 AI를 확산하기까지의 과정을 담았다. 상용 솔루션을 들였다가 10%대 사용률에 멈춰 선 일, 자체 플랫폼을 만들며 PoC에 갇힌 일, 전사 확산 단계에서 조직의 저항을 만난 일이 가감 없이 이어진다. 저자 박주혜, 오현식은 롯데그룹에서 AI 플랫폼과 거버넌스를 맡아 왔고, 공득조는 광주과학기술원(GIST) AI정책전략대학원 교수다.

이원준 영풍문고 기술부문 MD는 "4장 'ROI 없이 시작하고, ROI로 증명하기'와 5장 예산 확보 부분은 지금 사업계획서를 쓰는 담당자에게 그대로 필요한 내용"이라며 "경영진 보고를 숫자에서 이야기로 바꾸는 법까지 다룬다"고 말했다.

기술 쪽 기록도 구체적이다. 챗봇이 아니라 플랫폼이어야 하는 이유에서 출발해 여러 계열사를 한 플랫폼에 담는 멀티 테넌시, LLM 게이트웨이와 RAG 파이프라인, 권한 체계를 설계하고 아키텍처를 1.0에서 4.0까지 바꿔 온 과정을 보여 준다. 업무와 비용에 따라 모델을 나눠 쓰는 라우팅, 토큰 사용량 관리, 계열사별 데이터 격리 같은 운영 판단도 함께 담겼다. 기술팀과 기획팀이 같은 책을 펴 놓고 이야기할 수 있는 드문 AX 기록이다.

비슷한 책들과 놓고 보면 성격이 더 분명해진다. 영풍문고가 앞서 소개한 『CEO의 AI』가 경영자의 관점을, 『AI와 일하는 기술』이 개인의 활용법을 다뤘다면, 이 책은 그 사이에 있는 실무 조직의 시행착오를 기록한다. 같은 시기 나온 『일하는 AI 에이전트 설계하는 사람』이 에이전트에게 일을 맡기는 판단 기준에 집중한다면, 이 책은 플랫폼 아키텍처와 보안 거버넌스, 계열사별 배포, 3만 5,000명 온보딩까지 확산의 전 과정을 다룬다.

권기원 영풍문고 서적팀 팀장은 "AX 책 대부분이 방향을 말하는데, 이 책은 실패한 버전까지 남겼다는 점이 다르다"며 "유통, 제조, 서비스 사례가 산업별로 나뉘어 있어 자기 업종부터 찾아 읽기 좋다"고 덧붙였다.

items.title: "6G로 1800조원 창출, 주파수 부족 땐 750조원 손실”
items.summary: [지디넷코리아]6G 통신이 2040년 세계 경제에 1조 2400억 달러(약 1800조원)의 추가 가치를 창출할 것으로 전망됐다. 전 세계 국내총생산(GDP)의 0.7%에 해당하는 규모다. 주파수를 충분히 확보하지 못하면 경제효과의 최대 42%가 사라질 수 있다는 분석도 나왔다.5일(현지시간) 세계이동통신사업자연회(GSMA)는 '비전 2040: 6G의 경제적 편익' 보고서를 통해 6G 도입에 따른 산업별 경제효과와 주파수 부족에 따른 손실 가능성을 이같이 분석했다.보고서는 5G가 가장 발전된 이동통
items.content:
GSMA, 2030년까지 중대역 2GHz 확보 촉구

방송/통신 입력 :2026/11/06 08:45

6G 통신이 2040년 세계 경제에 1조 2400억 달러(약 1800조원)의 추가 가치를 창출할 것으로 전망됐다. 전 세계 국내총생산(GDP)의 0.7%에 해당하는 규모다. 주파수를 충분히 확보하지 못하면 경제효과의 최대 42%가 사라질 수 있다는 분석도 나왔다.

5일(현지시간) 세계이동통신사업자연회(GSMA)는 '비전 2040: 6G의 경제적 편익' 보고서를 통해 6G 도입에 따른 산업별 경제효과와 주파수 부족에 따른 손실 가능성을 이같이 분석했다.

보고서는 5G가 가장 발전된 이동통신 기술로 유지되는 상황과 비교해 6G가 추가로 창출할 경제적 가치를 추산했다. AI와 산업 자동화, 통신·센싱 융합, 위성통신 등이 주요 성장 동력으로 꼽혔다.

산업별로는 제조업이 전체 경제효과의 20%를 차지해 가장 큰 수혜를 볼 것으로 예상됐다. 금융서비스가 19%로 뒤를 이었고 건설업 13%, ICT 산업 12% 순으로 나타났다.

지역별 경제효과는 중화권이 3900억 달러로 가장 컸다. 북미는 2900억 달러, 유럽은 2250억 달러로 전망됐다.

GSMA는 6G가 AI를 네트워크 자체에 내재화하는 ‘AI 네이티브’ 기술로 발전할 것으로 내다봤다. 데이터 전송뿐 아니라 주변 환경을 감지하고 지능형 의사결정을 지원하며 지상망과 위성망을 통합하는 방식이다.

6G 경제효과의 70%는 중대역 주파수에서 발생할 것으로 예상됐다. 저대역 주파수도 약 25%를 담당할 전망이다. 중대역은 대용량 데이터 전송에, 저대역은 농어촌과 건물 내부 등 통신 음영지역 해소에 중요하다.

GSMA는 주파수 공급이 제한되면 2040년 최대 5200억 달러(약 750조원)의 경제적 가치가 사라질 수 있다고 경고했다. 이는 전체 예상 경제효과의 42%에 해당한다.

이에 따라 각국 정부에 2030년 전후까지 최소 2GHz 폭의 중대역 주파수를 확보할 것을 권고했다. 상위 6GHz 대역을 비롯해 3.5GHz, 4.5GHz, 7GHz 대역의 추가 공급이 필요하다고 제시했다. 저대역에서는 600MHz 대역 확보와 500MHz 대역 활용 검토를 주문했다.

GSMA는 2027년 세계전파통신회의(WRC-27)를 앞두고 국제적인 주파수 정책 공조도 촉구했다. 각국 정부가 명확한 주파수 공급 계획을 마련해야 통신사업자의 6G 투자와 상용화를 뒷받침할 수 있다는 설명이다.

존 주스티 GSMA 최고규제책임자는 “차세대 이동통신 기술은 AI를 뒷받침하고 산업을 변화시키며 경제 전반의 생산성을 새로운 수준으로 끌어올릴 것”이라며 “6G의 경제적 잠재력을 완전히 실현하려면 5000억 달러가 넘는 경제적 가치가 각국 정부의 주파수 정책 결정에 달려 있다”고 밝혔다.

보도에 따르면 닌텐도 경영진은 최근 실적 설명회에서 메모리 재고를 충분히 확보해 부품 가격 상승에 대응할 수 있다며, 당분간 스위치2 판매 가격을 추가로 인상할 계획은 없다고 설명했다.

닌텐도는 지난 9월 스위치2 미국 판매 가격을 기존 450달러(약 61만650원)에서 500달러(약 67만8500원)로 올린 바 있다. 앞서 플레이스테이션5와 엑스박스 시리즈 X·S도 가격이 올라 주요 콘솔 3종 모두 인상을 겪었다.

외신은 관세와 AI 기업들의 메모리·부품 수요 확대 등 거시경제 요인이 콘솔 가격 상승에 영향을 미쳤다고 분석했다. 또한 미국 중간선거 이후 기술주와 AI 관련 주식이 큰 폭으로 하락했지만, 메모리와 부품 시장 수급 부담이 언제 완화될지는 불확실하다고 전했다.

닌텐도는 이번 실적 발표에서 수백만달러 규모 관세 환급금을 받은 사실도 공개했다. 다만 이를 소비자에게 돌려주는 방식의 가격 인하는 발표하지 않았다.

items.content:
AI와 바이오 융합으로 빨라진 혁신…따라가기에 부족한 투자

헬스케어 입력 :2026/11/06 08:30

“반도체 뒤를 이을 산업은 바이오임은 확실하다. 하지만 현재 글로벌 수준에는 미흡하다”

반도체 성장 신화를 이을 산업으로 주목받는 제약바이오산업을 차세대 국가성장동력으로 발전시키기 위한 혁신을 모색하는 자리가 마련됐다.

국민경제자문회의, 국가과학기술자문회의, 국가바이오혁신위원회는 5일 오후 서울 코리아나호텔 그랜드볼룸에서 ‘대한민국 넥스트 엔진 : 바이오 대혁신, 국가미래성장을 잇다’를 주제로 공동포럼을 개최했다.

주제발표에 나선 묵현상 뉴패스바이오 대표는 바이오제약산업을 우리나라의 차세대 성장동력으로 육성하기 위한 투자 확대와 지원체계 개선 방안을 제시했다.

정부가 임상 등 기술이 제품화로 갈 수 있도록 지원을 확대하겠다고 밝혔지만, 정부 R&D 전체 규모의 확대에도 바이오분야는 상대적으로 비중이 작아지고 있어 제약바이오 R&D 투자 방식의 획기적 변화가 필요하다는 것이다.

묵 대표는 “2027년도 예산안을 보면 전년 대비 보건복지부의 보건의료연구개발은 -456억원, 보건산업진흥원 -906억원, 바이오헬스기술 개발은 -183억원 등 정작 임상·사업화에 대한 부처 예산이 오히려 줄었다”라며 “임상 2·3상 자금 공백은 그대로”라고 지적했다.

이어 “할 수 있는 기업에 투자를 하는 체계로 변해야 한다” “정부의 R&D 지원은 투자방식으로 하되 선정평가를 철저히 해 집중적 지원이 필요하고, 투자 대상을 선정할 때 공정성에 과도한 가중치(나눠먹기)와 경험 없는 대학교수들은 평가에서 배제하고 글로벌 전문가를 초빙해 평가위원으로 위촉하는 것도 필요하다”라고 밝혔다.

세부적으로 독성시험이나 임상1상 프로젝트에는 현재와 같이 R&D 지원으로 진행하되, 불성실 실패 시 정부 투자금을 전액 회수하거나 5년간 정부과제 응모를 금지하는 등의 제제가 필요하다고 밝혔다. 또 임상 2상, 3상 프로젝트의 경우 국내 5개 빅파마와 중소, 바이오벤처 등 공동프로젝트에 중점 투자하고 투자방식은 프로젝트 파이낸싱 방식을 제안했다.

운용주체 선정의 변화도 필요하다고 밝혔는데 VC의 경우 투자수익률을 핵심가치로 두기 때문에 정책 목표가 중요하지 않고, 정부가 직접 운용할 때는 VC 보다 보수적으로 운용할 가능성이 높다고 지적했다. 이에 미국 패밀리오피스 운용방식을 벤치마킹해 설계하는 방안을 제시하고, 바이오혁신위원회 산하 비공개 투자심의위원회 설립도 제안했다.

묵 대표는 “고수익, 일자리 등에서 볼 때 미래 핵심산업이 바이오제약임은 명확하지만, 기술수출로만 가치를 입증하려 해 글로벌 가치사슬에서 핵심을 놓치고 있다”라며 “온정주의를 버리고 냉정하게 가야한다”라고 말했다.

items.title: NASA unveils mysterious X-70 experimental aircraft using AI-generated image
items.summary: NASA’s X-70 Fractal announcement comes as agency aims to grow X-plane fleet.
items.content:
NASA has announced a new experimental aircraft, the X-70 Fractal, that will supposedly feature reconfigurable flight-control technology and a modular design for swapping in different payloads. But much remains unknown about the aircraft’s design and development timeline, even as NASA administrator Jared Isaacman said the X-plane could take flight within two years.

The mystery surrounding NASA’s newest X-plane was exemplified by the agency’s press release, including an apparently AI-generated image of the X-70, showing a dark silhouette vaguely resembling a military fighter jet obscured by smoke. The news was announced by Isaacman during the UP.Summit held at the agency’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida on November 4.

“The X-70 Fractal gives NASA a crewed, high-performance platform to test advanced flight-control, maneuverability, and other cutting-edge technologies in real flight,” Isaacman said. “Its modular design and ability to rapidly swap internal and external payloads will keep our teams flying, learning, and moving quickly from one experiment to the next.”

NASA’s press release described the X-70 as a crewed aircraft designed to cruise at Mach 0.75 while reaching a maximum altitude of up to 45,000 feet, and having an operational range beyond 1,726 miles (2,778 kilometers). The article did not mention a specific aircraft manufacturer that might be helping the agency develop the X-plane.

The X-70 would also have a takeoff weight of 10,000 pounds (4,536 kilograms) and a design capable of accommodating up to 2,000 pounds (907 kilograms) of experimental payloads both internally and externally. Ars has reached out to NASA for more details.

Another X-plane is also expected to be announced at the UP.Summit on November 6, according to Aviation Week . That would coincide with a scheduled announcement from President Donald Trump at the event.

This comes after Isaacman previously appeared in front of another smoke-shrouded silhouette image with the tagline “Rebuilding our X-plane portfolio” during the All-In Summit in Los Angeles held from September 12–14, according to TWZ . That silhouette appeared strikingly similar to the SR-71 Blackbird that flew Cold War reconnaissance missions at supersonic speeds in the stratosphere.

Rumors have circulated about a possible revival of the SR-71 in one form or another, after former NASA employees told Aviation Week they received job offers to help restore an SR-71 to operational flight capability.

In September, the publication also reported on the removal of a NASA-owned SR-71 with the tail number 844 that had stood on display at NASA’s Armstrong Flight Research Center inside Edwards Air Force Base in California.

Meanwhile, NASA recently commemorated the first flight anniversary of its supersonic X-59 Quesst, a needle-nosed aircraft designed by Lockheed Martin to reduce sonic booms to sonic thumps. Ars has previously looked at how this X-plane program is intended to support the design of future supersonic airliners that may fly overland while minimizing disturbances for buildings and people below.

Since first taking to the skies on October 28, 2025, the X-59 has completed over 40 flight tests, including both low-speed flights and supersonic test runs reaching Mach 1.53, according to NASA. Such testing has taken place at NASA’s Armstrong Flight Research Center inside Edwards Air Force Base in California.

The X-59 also recently completed its first cross-country journey from California to Florida with stopovers in Texas and Alabama, accompanied by an F-15 and an F/A-18 from the agency’s research fleet that served as chase planes. It sat on the ground as a static display during the NASA Max Power airshow at Kennedy Space Center in Florida from November 7–8.

The supersonic aircraft will resume its test flight schedule once it returns to Armstrong Flight Research Center in California, a NASA spokesperson told Ars. Given the agency’s latest X-plane push, the X-59 may not be flying alone for many more years.

items.title: Airbnb says it’s launching an AI travel agent in the first half of 2027
items.summary: Airbnb says its upcoming AI agent will help travelers plan trips, compare options, manage bookings, and get assistance throughout their stay.
items.content:
Airbnb has teased its plans to build its own AI travel agent before, but on Thursday the company announced that the new AI feature will launch in the first half of 2027. In the company’s Q3 shareholder letter on Thursday , Airbnb also provided more detail about how the agent will work, what it will actually do, and how it’s different from a typical AI chatbot.

In prior interviews, CEO Brian Chesky sketched out the travel company’s approach to AI, describing a plan to build an AI agent that has a richer interface than a conventional chatbot. He also expressed his opinions about how chatbots aren’t the right interface for travel, noting that people take pleasure in the planning process and in anticipating a trip. Any agent that it built, then, shouldn’t take away from the inspiration and the browsing, he told TechCrunch in an interview last month.

Chesky today reiterated that belief, telling analysts on the earnings call that people won’t use one AI agent for everything.

“Today’s AI agents like Muse and Instinct are good at simple routine tasks like making a restaurant reservation or scheduling an appointment. But planning a trip is different,” he said. “Travel is aspirational. Discovering where to go and where to stay is part of the experience. In fact, 80% of travelers say they enjoy spending time researching trips. People want to look at photos. They want to compare homes. They want to make decisions with people they’re traveling with,” he continued. “And I don’t think the general-purpose agents are the best to do that. So that is why we are building our own AI agent,” Chesky said.

Airbnb described its agent as having a personalized interface that’s designed specifically for travel, where it will “build an interface” around a user’s question instead of simply responding as a chatbot would.

“What we are doing is developing a custom-designed AI-native experience that responds to what guests are looking for,” Chesky said. “So instead of relying on traditional chat alone, which is very text-heavy — which, again, is definitely not the way you should plan travel, our agent draws from a library of hundreds of travel-specific interface components — maps, photos, comparisons, calendars, itineraries — and composes them in real time to match what they’re looking for.”

The exec said the agent will feel “a little bit like generative UI” as it’s designed to offer up “the right interface at the right time” for someone’s specific travel needs.

In its shareholder letter, the company touted that its nearly 20 years of experience in bringing hosts and guests together is informing how the agent is built, as it incorporates insights about how people both book and host on its platform. The agent will also be able to help travelers beyond the booking itself.

“Our agent will be able to help guests throughout their trip — from changing a reservation or resolving a payment issue to getting help with refunds, rebooking, or 24-hour safety support. These are things an outside agent can’t easily do on its own,” the company wrote.

Over time, Airbnb expects the agent will be able to help travelers with other aspects of their trip, including not only homes and hotels, but also services and experiences. Services and experiences are two areas that have become a bigger focus for the company following its redesign last year.

While the company previously said to expect its AI agent sometime in the next year, it’s now more specifically committing to roll out the new technology to consumers in the first half of 2027.

The news of the agent’s release was delivered alongside strong third-quarter earnings, with revenue growing 19% to $4.87 billion, topping Wall Street estimates. It also raised its 2026 revenue growth forecast, which it now predicts will be in the high teens, instead of the mid-teens.

“Airbnb is back in growth mode,” Chesky told analysts on the Q3 earnings call on Thursday. “It’s rare for a marketplace of our size to reaccelerate growth, but that’s exactly what we’re doing. Q3 was our fastest revenue growth in more than three years,” he added.

items.content:
쓸 수 없고 분절된 데이터 의미 없어…글로벌과 협력·공유 가능한 데이터 만들어야

IT 일반 입력 :2026/11/06 07:30

“쓸 수 없고 분절된 데이터 의미 없다”

국민경제자문회의, 국가과학기술자문회의, 국가바이오혁신위원회는 5일 오후 서울 코리아나호텔 그랜드볼룸에서 ‘대한민국 넥스트 엔진 : 바이오 대혁신, 국가미래성장을 잇다’를 주제로 공동포럼을 열고 제약바이오산업이 차세대 국가성장동력으로 발전하기 위한 방안을 모색했다.

이현숙 서울대학교 교수는 ‘AI 데이터 기반 바이오 혁신전략’을 주제로 한 발표에서 “AI-Bio라는 새로운 무기는 데이터 없이 장착할 수 없다. 한국에는 사업은 있지만 패키지가 부족하다. GPU, AI 모델만큼, AI가 학습할 바이오 데이터에도 묶음 투자가 필요하다”라며 제약바이오 데이터 활용을 위한 지원을 강조했다.

이 교수는 “AI가 바로 학습하고 판단하는 데 활용할 수 있는 고품질 바이오, 의료데이터가 필요하지만 한국의 바이오 데이터 인프라는 부처별, 기관별 따로 자라왔다. 즉 데이터는 있지만 AI가 쓸 수 있는 형태는 아니다. 데이터는 계속 나오는데 이러한 데이터를 쓸 수 있도록 표준화하기 위해 많은 비용이 필요하다”라고 지적했다.

이어 “건강보험 데이터가 있다고 말할 것이 아니라 활용이 가능해야 한다. 모두가 쓸 수 없는 데이터는 글로벌 협력도 힘들고, 우리 데이터만으로 바이오 강국으로 가기는 힘들다”라며 “협력하기 위해서는 데이터 양 보다는 활용 가능한지, 기관 간 통합이 가능한지가 중요하다. 지금부터는 선진 모델로, 한번에 돌아가는 공진화의 엔진으로 가야 한다”라고 밝혔다.

특히 “데이터를 공개해 더 많이 쓸 수 있는 허브에 우리도 들어가야 한다. 우리는 시작도 안 했는데 바이오 경쟁국은 데이터를 열 곳과 닫을 곳을 구분하기 시작했다”라며 “공공바이오 R&D 투자나 신약 기술수출 규모에서는 (글로벌과) 체급이 다르다. 빨리 들어가기 위해서는 선진국과 교환할 수 있는 양질의 데이터를 만들어야 한다”라고 강조했다.

#. 바이오 데이터는 실험에서 나온 국가 자산…실패까지 학습해야 경쟁력

이 교수는 실패한 데이터의 활용도 중요하다고 강조했다. 그는 “임상에 진입한 후보물질의 실패율은 90%이다. 가장 많은 정보가 실패에 있는 것”이라며 “성공한 것만 학습한 AI는 경쟁력이 없다. 남이 갖지 못한 실패까지 학습한 모델의 경쟁력이 더 커지기 때문에 이를 활용하는 것이 숙제”라고 말했다.

이에 실패한 데이터 확보를 위한 유인책으로 ▲기업 실패 데이터 유인책 마련 ▲국가 R&D의 실패, 음성 결과도 데이터관리계획(DMP)에 등록 의무화 ▲실패 데이터 기여를 연구 성과로 인정하고 평가지표에 반영 ▲기업 실패 데이터 유인책 마련(민관 합작) 등을 제안했다.

그는 “바이오 데이터는 사오는 것이 아니라 실험으로 길러내는 국가 자산이다. 때문에 정부는 데이터의 양보다 질문의 발굴, 인재 양성과 귀한 데이터 누적에 투자해야 한다”라며 “필요한 것은 부처별 릴레이가 아니라 데이터-예산-성과가 함께 흐르는 하나의 루프이다. 보호는 그대로, 절차는 한번에, 안전한 분석환경 안에서는 빠르게 쓰게 하는 것이 경쟁력”이라고 말했다.

반면 경쟁력 있는 제약바이오 데이터 구축을 위해 ▲예산(데이터는 R&D 비용인가) ▲법제도(규제가 활용을 막는가) ▲거버넌스(누가 책임지는가) ▲안보(무엇을 지킬 것인가) 등 4가지를 허들로 지목했다.

이 교수는 “반도체 다음이 바이오라고 한다. 내가 21년째 제약바이오를 차세대 국가성장동력이라는 이야기를 듣고 있지만 투자와 지속적인 성장동력이 마련되고 있는지는 의문”이라며 “국내에서는 연결하고 밖으로는 신뢰하는 글로벌 스탠다드에 맞는 바이오 데이터 외교가 필요하다“라고 강조했다.

이와 함께 글로벌 바이오 강국을 위해 ▲AI R&D와 피지컬 AI 투자와 연동된 바이오 R&D 투자확대로 지속적인 미래 성장동력 확보 ▲신약과 AI의료 미션별 데이터 로드맵을 기획 단계부터 설계 ▲국가연구데이터법 시행 전에 AI-Ready 기준 수립 필요 ▲성공-실패 데이터 생산과 디스커버리의 낙수효과 체계 ▲연구와 GPU 투자를 묶어서 투자 ▲AI-Bio 연구소 허브화(전국을 묶고 기업을 연결) ▲데이터 안보와 글로벌 협력(안에서는 빠르게 쓰고 밖으로는 우방국과 상호 인정) ▲부처간 분절 없는 R&D 등을 제언했다.

items.content:
Like OpenAI’s Dots and Claude Duet, Perplexity’s Teammates can perform an array of tasks while running 24/7.

Perplexity is taking on OpenAI and Anthropic with its own work-focused AI agents. The startup’s new always-on “Teammates” can take on multiple roles within a workspace, while pulling existing projects, skills, and memory from the Perplexity tools you already use.

Teammates integrate with Perplexity Computer , an AI system that can deploy agents on your device to complete tasks. But Perplexity says Teammates “build on top” of Computer by offering the ability to collaborate and complete “ongoing, large-scale work.” You can assign each Teammate different jobs that they can perform simultaneously — much like OpenAI’s Dots and Claude Duet . Perplexity’s take on the feature is much more expensive, however, as it requires a subscription to its $200 / month Max plan.

Perplexity notes that you can keep tabs on Teammates’ progress through individual threads in the Perplexity app, as well as interact with them in Slack. “Over time, we envision every org having hundreds of teammates working for each person,” Perplexity CEO Aravind Srinivas says on X .

items.content:
Salon says its publishing model is ‘no longer sustainable.’

Salon launched 31 years ago as one of the first online-only news magazine outlets, and it announced today in an unsigned post that it’s ceasing publication.

The company said that the “business realities of independent digital journalism have changed profoundly over the years,” and it decided that its publishing model is “no longer sustainable.” It didn’t go into detail about why, but many websites are grappling with “Google Zero” and the impact of AI tools . When reached for comment, Salon general manager Amanda Wolfe pointed The Verge to today’s announcement post.

“Thirty-one years is a remarkable run, but what matters most is what happened during those years: the journalism, the ideas, the voices, the conversations and the community that grew around them,” Salon said in its post. “Salon helped demonstrate what digital journalism could be and could become. We hope that legacy will continue to matter long after today.”

On Bluesky, Salon chief content officer Erin Keane says that the editorial archive will “stay live for now.”

Current Salon owner Find.co acquired Salon in 2023 and describes itself as a “Performance Marketing Ecosystem transforming crypto marketing with performance and precision.”

핵심과제 TF 구성·운영계획·입법 방향 심의…공공 데이터 활용과 국방 AI도 안건

컴퓨팅 입력 :2026/11/06 07:00 수정: 2026/11/06 08:37

국가 인공지능(AI) 전략을 실행과 성과로 연결하겠다고 밝힌 하정우 국가인공지능전략위원회 상근부위원장이 취임 후 첫 전체회의에 나선다. AI 행동계획 확정 8개월여 만에 주요 과제를 추진할 조직과 법·제도 정비 방향을 논의할 예정이다.

국가AI전략위는 6일 오후 3시 서울스퀘어에서 제3차 전체회의를 연다. 국가 AI 핵심과제 추진을 위한 태스크포스(TF) 구성·운영계획과 대한민국 인공지능 입법 프레임워크 등을 심의·의결할 전망이다. 공공 데이터를 AI에 활용하는 방안과 국방 분야에서 AI를 독자적으로 개발·운영하는 추진계획도 다룬다.

이번 회의에서는 주요 AI 과제를 맡을 전담 조직을 어떻게 꾸리고 운영할지 논의할 것으로 보인다. 하 부위원장은 지난 9월 위원회를 프로젝트와 성과 중심으로 개편하겠다고 예고했다. 반도체와 피지컬 AI, AI 데이터센터 등 대형 사업을 연결하고 여러 부처에 걸친 업무를 조율하겠다는 구상이었다.

AI 관련 법·제도를 어떤 방향으로 정비할지도 심의한다. 법률TF가 설명할 '대한민국 인공지능 입법 프레임워크(안)'이 해당 안건이다. 위원회는 지난 2차 회의에서 부처별 AI 입법 방향을 조율하기 위해 법률TF를 만들겠다고 밝혔다.

조직과 제도 논의에 이어 공공·국방 분야 추진계획을 다룬다. 행정안전부는 부처별로 나뉜 데이터를 연결하는 '범정부 데이터 파이프라인' 구축 현황과 활용 방안을 설명한다. 데이터를 연결하는 작업이 어디까지 진행됐고, 이를 AI 개발과 공공서비스에 어떻게 활용할지 논의할 예정이다.

국방부는 '국방 소버린 AI 구현을 위한 추진계획'을 제시한다. 국방 분야에서 필요한 AI를 스스로 개발하고 운영할 역량을 확보하는 내용이다. 하 부위원장은 취임 당시 수출 통제 등으로 외국 기술을 쓰기 어려워질 가능성을 언급하며 국방과 공공 등 안보상 중요한 분야에서 독자 AI 역량을 갖춰야 한다고 강조했다.

위원회는 지난해 9월 1차 전체회의에서 AI 액션플랜 추진 방향을 논의하고 올해 2월 25일 2차 회의에서 대한민국 인공지능행동계획을 확정했다. 행동계획에는 99개 실행과제와 326개 정책 권고사항을 담았다. 이번에는 과제를 추진할 조직과 입법 방향, 분야별 추진계획을 안건으로 올렸다.

하 부위원장은 지난 8월 31일 취임 간담회에서 부처 간 쟁점을 조정하고 데이터 활용과 데이터센터 인허가 등 현장 문제를 해결하겠다고 밝혔다. 부처별 AI 정책 평가와 예산 검토를 정책 실행 수단으로 제시하기도 했다.

국가AI전략위는 대통령 직속 기구로 지난해 9월 출범했다. 민간 전문가와 정부가 함께 국가 AI 전략을 세우고 부처별 정책을 조율하는 국가 AI 정책 컨트롤타워 역할을 맡는다.

하 부위원장은 9월 성과보고회에서 "이제는 지난 1년간 마련한 기반을 국민과 기업이 체감하는 변화로 이어가는 것이 무엇보다 중요하다"며 "저와 함께하는 2기 위원회는 부처와 분야의 벽을 넘어 필요한 역량을 연결하고 현장 걸림돌을 해소하는 데 더욱 힘쓰겠다"고 말했다.

items.content:
3일(현지시간) 미국 중간선거와 함께 실시된 AI 데이터센터 관련 주민투표 결과입니다. 미국 10개 주에서 상정된 41건 가운데 4일 집계에서 결과가 확인된 40건 중 39건에서 데이터센터 건설 제한을 지지하거나 개발 허용에 반대하는 결과가 나왔습니다. 노스다코타주 하우드에서만 규제 강화안이 부결됐습니다.

이처럼 미국 유권자들이 데이터센터 건설에 압도적인 반대 의사를 나타내면서 AI가 이번 중간선거의 주요 쟁점으로 떠올랐다는 평가가 나오고 있습니다. 뉴욕타임스(NYT) 는 이번 선거를 유권자들이 AI에 대한 엄격한 검토를 요구한 사건으로 다뤘습니다. 로이터 는 데이터센터 반대 세력의 정치적 영향력이 확인됐다고 분석했으며, 워싱턴포스트 는 AI와 데이터센터가 올해 처음으로 주요 선거운동 쟁점에 올랐다고 전했습니다.

주민들의 반발은 주로 전기요금 상승과 막대한 전력·용수 사용, 소음, 환경 문제에 집중됐습니다. AI 기술 자체보다는 데이터센터 건설에 따른 지역사회의 부담과 개발 절차에 불만을 제기한 것입니다. S&P글로벌 자료에 따르면, 올해 8월 초까지 미국에서는 145개 이상의 데이터센터 프로젝트가 지연되거나 취소됐으며 대부분 주민 반대가 원인이었습니다.

데이터센터 규제를 공약한 후보들도 주지사 선거에서 승리했습니다. 텍사스에서는 신규 데이터센터 승인 중단을 공약한 민주당의 지나 이노호사가 공화당 소속 그레그 애벗 주지사를 꺾었습니다. 조지아에서도 데이터센터 규제를 내세운 민주당의 키샤 랜스 보텀스가 승리했으며, 오하이오에서는 민주당의 에이미 액턴이 주지사에 당선됐습니다. 공화당 지지 지역에서도 데이터센터 건설에 반대하는 움직임이 나타났습니다.

이번 선거 결과로 일부 지역에서는 신규 데이터센터 건설이 실제로 제한됩니다. 미국 로펌 베너블 에 따르면, 메인주 일부 지역에서는 신규 인허가를 6개월간 중단하는 조치가 통과됐고, 오하이오주 일부 도시에서는 데이터센터 건설이 금지됐습니다. 또 위스콘신주 제인스빌에서는 80억달러 규모의 데이터센터 개발 사업을 포함해 일정 규모 이상의 프로젝트에 주민투표를 의무화하는 조치가 통과됐습니다. 그러나 일부 주민투표는 법적 구속력이 없는 의견 조사이며, 이번 결과로 미국 전역의 기존 데이터센터 건설이 일괄 중단되는 것은 아닙니다.

파이낸셜타임스(FT) 에 따르면, 일론 머스크를 비롯해 벤처캐피털 앤드리슨호로위츠, 오픈AI 공동 창업자 그렉 브록먼 등이 참여한 공화당 지원 캠페인에 6억달러 이상이 투입됐습니다. 그러나 민주당이 상·하원에서 모두 승리했으며, 기술 업계가 후원한 일부 주요 후보들도 낙선했습니다. 다만 이 자금에는 데이터센터 정책뿐 아니라 암호화폐와 세금 등 다양한 정책적 이해관계가 포함됐습니다.

규제 강화 움직임은 투자와 의회 정책에도 영향을 미칠 전망입니다. 골드만삭스는 데이터센터 규제가 강화될 가능성이 있는 주에 미국의 신규 데이터센터 계획 용량 중 약 45%가 집중돼 있다고 분석했습니다. 월스트리트저널(WSJ) 은 민주당이 AI 기업 경영진을 의회에 소환해 트럼프 행정부와의 관계를 조사하는 방안을 검토하고 있다고 보도했습니다.

데이터센터가 지역사회에 제공하는 혜택을 충분히 설명하지 못했다는 평가도 나왔습니다. 매사추세츠대학교의 타티셰 은테타 정치학 교수는 악시오스 인터뷰 에서 AI 기업들이 주민들을 설득하는 데 실패했다고 지적했습니다. 기업들도 주민 반발에 대응하고 있습니다. 아마존과 마이크로소프트, 구글 등 하이퍼스케일러들은 물론, 메타와 오픈AI, 앤트로픽 등 AI 개발 기업들도 주민을 위한 정책을 잇달아 내놓고 있습니다.

AI 업계는 이미 2028년 대통령 선거를 겨냥한 정책 논의에도 나섰습니다. 오픈AI의 크리스 리헤인 글로벌 정책 책임자는 중간 선거가 끝나자마자 ' 2028년: AI 선거 '라는 글을 내놓고 차기 대선의 가장 중요한 쟁점이 AI가 될 것이라고 전망했습니다. 그는 이번 선거에서 데이터센터가 생활비 부담과 거대 기업의 영향력에 대한 불만을 상징하게 됐다며, 정치인들이 AI 안전성과 일자리, 생활비 등에 관한 구체적인 정책을 제시해야 한다고 주장했습니다.

특히 리헤인은 데이터센터 건설 중단이 미국의 AI 경쟁력을 약화시키고 중국에 주도권을 내주는 결과로 이어질 수 있다고 경고했습니다. 사우스차이나모닝포스트(SCMP) 도 미국의 데이터센터 건설이 지연되면 중국의 AI 개발에 유리한 환경이 조성될 수 있다는 전문가들의 분석을 전했습니다.

과연 이번 선거가 미국의 데이터센터 건설과 AI 산업에 어떤 영향을 미칠지 주목됩니다.

■ "저가 칩에 HBM 숨겨 중국으로"...삼성·SK 메모리 밀반입 수법 드러나

삼성전자와 SK하이닉스의 고대역폭메모리(HBM)를 저성능 서버 프로세서에 결합해 미국의 수출 규제를 우회한 뒤 중국에서 메모리만 분리하는 밀수 수법이 드러났습니다. 특히 국내 반도체 업계에서 오랫동안 일하며 쌓은 인맥과 경험을 활용해 밀수에 관여한 인물도 있는 것으로 전해졌습니다.

■ 오픈AI, AI로 하드웨어 설계 일주일 만에 완료…실제 시제품 제작

오픈AI가 'GPT-6 아스트라'를 활용해 전자 부품 선정부터 회로기판과 소프트웨어 설계까지 수행하고, 일주일도 안 돼 설계를 마친 하드웨어의 시제품을 실제 제작했습니다. AI가 소프트웨어를 넘어 실제 기기의 설계까지 맡기 시작하면서, 하드웨어 개발에서도 AI의 역할이 커질 가능성을 보여줬습니다.

■ "AI에 일 맡길수록 감독 능력도 퇴화"…앤트로픽 엔지니어 경고

클로드 코드 개발팀 엔지니어 애디 오스마니가 AI 에이전트에 업무를 맡길수록 인간의 전문성과 결과물 검증 능력까지 약해질 수 있다는 '감독의 역설'을 경고했습니다. AI의 답변이 점점 정확하고 그럴듯해지면서 이용자가 검증을 소홀히 할 수 있다며, 비판적 사고와 직접 문제를 해결하는 경험을 유지해야 한다고 강조했습니다.

items.title: Google: Schools can keep search while skipping Gemini, but AI search is non-negotiable
items.summary: Google is technically offering schools more choice but not the choices anyone wants.
items.content:
Google faced the ire of educators and parents earlier this week when it announced a new AI policy for K–12 schools . Google said that it developed its new approach to give schools more control, but early reporting also suggested Google would block search access for schools that didn’t want to use AI. Google didn’t see the backlash coming, but now that it’s here, the search giant is clarifying what exactly its new policy means and what’s changing.

The gist of the new policy, according to Google’s blog post, is that schools using Google apps will have to opt into its AI products going forward. Since the company considers search part of its AI portfolio (Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Search), schools have to specifically turn that on for logged-in student accounts.

When Google revealed its new policy, the company’s VP for education spoke exclusively to The New York Times , which interpreted the situation as Google will “turn off search” if schools reject AI. This has a nefarious vibe, but it’s probably not the most accurate way to describe how Google’s educational AI system will operate. Google’s approach may not be entirely altruistic, but it technically offers schools more choice and control than they have now. Instead of Google turning off search, it will let schools make that decision based on their internal AI policies.

The company clarified in a tweet that it will allow schools to disable Gemini apps while leaving search active for students. If they don’t want any AI, they can leave it all off. Essentially, Google is giving schools that want to completely block AI the ability to go all the way, even removing search from student accounts.

A Google spokesperson tells Ars that the company has not made any changes to the new policy it announced this week. However, the vagueness of Google’s blog post and public statements didn’t fully explain what it plans to do. There are still reasons to dislike Google’s approach, but here’s how the company explains the process for schools:

As things currently stand, schools can block the Gemini app, but the AI tools in search (AI Overviews and AI Mode) are still present and offer many of the same intellectual shortcuts. When schools choose which AI features to use under this new system, search will be one of the options. Schools can leave search off if they want, but opting in will require them to choose the standard AI features or the new Guided Learning version, which won’t give away answers as readily (or so Google claims).

Schools are gaining the ability to block Google’s AI tools, even those in search, while keeping other Google apps. Notably, the company’s new approach to “responsible AI for learning” does not include the ability to use search without AI. So schools get more control, even if they don’t get the AI-free search everyone seems to want.

Many will argue that Google should let schools access web search without chatbots. However, that’s just not something Google wants to support at any level because it sees AI as the future of search. While other search engines have settings to turn off AI tools, Google steadfastly refuses to create such a toggle (and those no-AI tricks you rely on may not work forever). Ultimately, this is the core problem not just for education customers, but for everyone who wants to limit their exposure to AI while using Google.

This clarification does not change the calculus for educators who want to allow students to search the Internet without AI tools. Google won’t offer that, and switching to another provider is easier said than done. Google still has by far the most expansive index of the Internet, leaving alternatives with numerous gaps. That may change in the near future, though. As a result of Google’s loss in the DOJ’s search antitrust case , it will have to provide competitors limited access to its index of the web. This could give other provides a chance to improve and offer a more viable alternative to Google.

items.title: Lawsuit: Man introduced his wife to ChatGPT. She used it to plan his murder.
items.summary: Bitter energy drinks turned out to be ChatGPT-steered poisoning, lawsuit says.
items.content:
ChatGPT allegedly helped a North Carolina woman, Cheryl Gates, craft a “personalized plan” to poison her husband, James, after fueling her delusions that he planned to divorce her and leave her with nothing.

A grand jury indicted Cheryl Gates on charges of attempted first-degree murder and food contamination in October. About a week prior, the accusations that ChatGPT was a co-conspirator in the attempted murder came in a lawsuit filed in San Francisco County Superior Court that was made public this week. In it, James Gates alleged that OpenAI and Sam Altman failed to employ technical safeguards to shut down Cheryl’s chats even after her queries became “obviously suspicious” and sought advice on how to execute and conceal a homicide.

At first, Cheryl told ChatGPT that she was researching poisoning out of fear that her husband might possibly try to kill her—framing her queries as “self-protection.” Coming to the rescue, ChatGPT did not terminate the conversation. Instead, it helped her “with specific instructions for the preparation, dosage, and administration of Oleander, including whether anti-nausea medicine would accelerate or inhibit death, whether it would show on an autopsy report, and whether it could be injected into a vein or muscle instead of being ingested in tea and have the same lethal effect,” the lawsuit said.

Cheryl continued probing poisoning plans in at least 25 different exchanges, but eventually it became clear that James was the target of the poisoning, the lawsuit said. Over time, she shifted to telling the chatbot that she needed to know “how much would be pretty much instantly fatal by injection—to me OR HIM.” Among queries that could have been flagged as homicidal, she asked ChatGPT if a “0.2mg for a 200-pound man for clonidine is lethal—by itself?”

“Instead of referring Cheryl to law enforcement, therapeutic services, a poison control agency, or discontinuing the conversation, ChatGPT repeatedly calculated the lethal dosages for each medication available in the home based on a subject weighing approximately 200 pounds,” the lawsuit said.

Once Cheryl finished researching the drugs, the chats focused on how to hide the poison so James would ingest it without detecting it. In a chat labeled “Why Celsius Would Be More ‘Stealth’ for Drugging,” ChatGPT explained that the energy drink Celsius would be more likely to mask the bitter taste of the Oleander or other crushed-up drugs than beer or soda, if James drank it in the morning.

“It is physically possible to pierce a sealed soda can with a syringe in a way that could allow someone to inject a substance without obvious signs,” ChatGPT explained, while adding that “in dark, sweet sodas, the bitterness might be masked,” but “Celsius actually hides those powders better.”

Cheryl allegedly repeatedly attempted to poison her husband between June and September 2025. As she grew thinner and unrecognizable, seemingly spending 24 hours a day on ChatGPT, James had noticed that his Celsius drinks tasted bitter. He even tossed out a can he left unattended after beginning to suspect his wife may be messing with his drinks. During the most serious attempt, he was sick for 72 hours, experiencing “cardiac symptoms, extreme jitteriness, shooting abdominal pain, severe weakness, and confusion so profound he could not form coherent text messages.” He was so out of it, he didn’t notice his 6-year-old son recording a video that captured his troubling illness.

But it wasn’t until he found a handwritten note documenting “Things hidden” in the house and referencing a toxic combination of “oleander, clonidine, clonazepam, pregabalin, nifedipine, and Atenolo” that he called police, who urgently investigated and exposed the chat logs. At the top of that note, Cheryl wrote, “clear all convos” and “log out of ChatGPT,” the lawsuit said. After listing dosages, delivery methods, and drug combinations, her note also listed outcomes such as “blackout if ingest” and “lethal.”

“These conversations revealed that ChatGPT did not just mechanically provide publicly available knowledge to Cheryl, it crafted a personalized plan to help her commit and get away with murder,” the lawsuit alleged.

Suing Altman personally, the lawsuit also alleged that the OpenAI CEO prioritized profits over safety by relaxing safeguards that would have blocked outputs on illegal drugs. OpenAI justified that by arguing that ChatGPT shouldn’t be “judgy” or “preachy” when asked about a certain drug, but James alleged the example it provided for “when a user asks about drug use” was “eerily similar in tone to the conversations Cheryl had with the model.”

Asked for comment, an OpenAI spokesperson told Ars that “safety is a top priority. We banned this user and have provided information to law enforcement as part of their investigation into this case.”

OpenAI has worked with mental health experts to help detect chats where vulnerable users form potentially dangerous emotional dependencies on ChatGPT.

However, James said that his now-estranged wife “didn’t fit the mold of a ‘vulnerable’ user, but she was vulnerable nonetheless.”

“We all are at some point,” James said. “She took her grievances about our marriage to ChatGPT and months of engagement drove her farther and farther from herself—and from reality. She became someone I no longer recognized. And I became someone she wanted dead. For almost a year, I couldn’t make sense of her actions. Then I read her chat logs. She didn’t act alone.”

James Gates is a cybersecurity professional who recently celebrated his 10-year anniversary with his wife, Cheryl. For much of their marriage, Cheryl was a stay-at-home mom to their two children, but two years previously, she’d gone back to work, as the family was experiencing some financial struggles.

items.title: Ads in Chatbots Have Arrived. Here’s What’s Working—and What’s Not
items.summary: As Anthropic maintains its vow to keep ads out of Claude, the rest of the AI chatbot industry is racing to win over advertisers without antagonizing users.
items.content:
Anthropic is holding firm on the pledge made in its Super Bowl commercial this year to keep Claude ad-free. The company’s recent IPO filing didn’t even mention the possibility of selling ads to make money from the AI chatbot. It’s easy to maintain the high ground with about $112 billion in investor cash.

The chatbot industry, though, may find selling ads necessary to defray the high costs of generating AI responses . OpenAI is all in, with over 100,000 customers advertising in ChatGPT since ads debuted there in February. Last week, Google expanded ads in its search chatbot AI Mode to 10 more countries beyond the US and declared that users “find them highly relevant.” Advertisers are far from satisfied with the experience, but they expect it to improve.

Ads stand to be particularly vital for the long-term viability of niche chatbot platforms, which can’t rely on the same degree of venture capital largesse as the top AI labs or the massive revenues of tech giants. I recently spoke with Koah Labs, one of a number of new ad technology companies focused on AI experiences . The San Francisco startup markets itself as bringing ads to over 200 apps, such as DeepAI, which offers tools for creative queries, and Liner, which focuses on providing citations in AI answers. It works with brands like telehealth giant Hims and flower delivery service UrbanStems.

Koah has attracted just a tenth of the advertisers OpenAI has, but CEO Nic Baird still believes he’s getting a good sense of what’s working and what’s fuzzy as chatbots take over from traditional search engines—and what their rise will mean for your AI experiences.

Ads composed partly by AI rather than fully by a human generate double the clicks, Baird says. It’s difficult to assess exactly why, but AI-generated marketing copy likely feels more natural next to the output of an AI model.

Because ads shown by Koah are grounded in product details and imagery supplied by the advertiser, users don’t seem to be encountering AI-hallucinated, erroneous information. But some advertisers, such as drugmakers, face government requirements on what they must—or cannot—say in ads, Baird says. These companies default to more human control over their ads, generating weaker results, according to Baird.

Since ads with dull messages or that feel like clutter could drive users away, the onus is on ad tech companies to find a middle ground that’s engaging to users without triggering risk-averse brands. That balance might be harder to strike when a human is out of the loop.

Google searches for “help with stress” are likely to bring up ads for therapists. Chatbots can get more creative, in Baird’s view. For instance, ads for spas have performed well within Koah’s network when shown after users’ prompts related to “stress,” he says.

The key difference, according to Baird, is that Koah can select and customize the ad based on “not only the prompt, or the Google search, but also the response from the AI platform, which brings context from the rest of the conversation thus far.” In addition, chatbot prompts tend to be at least double the length of Google queries, giving Koah more information to determine a relevant ad.

Baird claims users are accustomed to navigating through multiple topics within a chatbot conversation, which could make them more receptive to adjacent marketing than they are in traditional search. Koah says users are clicking on about 3 percent of ads, about on par with the performance of the more mature Google ads system.

When called on to show an ad, Koah generally receives a user’s entire conversation up to that point to help inform what it displays. While traditional search queries generally look for specific information, people often use chatbots as not just conversation partners but confidants. It’s unclear whether users will accept the privacy trade-offs that come with personalized chatbot ads as they begin to proliferate.

Baird says Koah anonymizes the queries it receives and stores them in a de-identified way, but he declined to comment any further on the data collection and storage. While acknowledging that personalization can become intrusive, he argues that there are benefits for users and advertisers alike as the tech matures. Nonsensitive information about chatbot discussions, for instance, could inform personalized content on the page that loads after an ad click. Perhaps someone expressed interest in a specific feature, or the AI model didn’t highlight a particular downside of a competing product. The advertiser could fill in the gap.

Koah doesn’t have data on whether people actually want these customized pages, but the tech industry has long argued that people prefer when ad experiences feel relevant. Having the conversation history also could benefit advertisers when Koah enables retargeting, or repeating, an ad to the same user.

By Koah’s estimate, one out of every four chatbot queries about a retailer or brand concerns a return, exchange, or other support issue. Baird believes chatbots provide an opportunity not replicated easily elsewhere for advertisers to address what they might politely call a “customer success” matter.

He expects manufacturers and retailers will eventually target disappointed customers to remind them about warranties, engage them in an AI-intermediated support, and potentially steer them away from a more costly customer service interaction. It’s possible that the AI chatbot’s response may provide users with similar help, but buying an ad guarantees companies get their message across.

The ideal outcome is users reaching resolution they can live with more swiftly than through other means. In the worst case, it's a wasted ad buy and a more irate consumer.

items.title: Serve Robotics launches new business to become the AWS for robots
items.summary: Serve Robotics announced alonsgside its third-quarter earnings that it will launch a new business line called Physical AI Services to offer customers its connectivity and data tools.
items.content:
Serve Robotics , a maker of self-driving sidewalk delivery robots, is expanding beyond its autonomous delivery operations in a bid to become a technology supplier to other companies building robots.

The company, which spun out of Uber’s acquisition of Postmates in 2021 and went public in 2024, said Thursday it will launch a new business line called Physical AI Services.

Specifically, Serve Robotics will offer customers its connectivity and data tools. Bedrock Robotics, a startup developing self-driving systems for construction equipment, is a customer, according to Serve. It’s also working with T-Mobile to bring AI computing power closer to robots, Serve announced alongside its third-quarter earnings on Thursday.

“We are solving the problem of robots in human spaces,” Serve Robotics CEO and co-founder Ali Kashani told TechCrunch.

Serve Robotics already makes two kinds of robots, the cute googly-eyed sidewalk delivery robot and one designed for hospitals that it got through its acquisition of Diligent Robotics .

Those businesses are not going away, Kashani emphasized in a recent interview. Instead, he said there is opportunity to sell the technology it developed for its own robots to other companies developing robots for farms, warehouses, and other uncontrolled environments.

“I kind of think of it as the AWS moment where we are taking the technology we’ve built for us, and we’re opening it up for more people to build on,” he said, adding this wouldn’t have been possible without developing its own robot fleet.

The expansion comes as Serve’s sidewalk delivery business expands, but is shifting away from Uber and toward other partners, including DoorDash and Wonder.

Its new Physical AI Services business line will offer three products. Serve Link helps connect robots in the field to AI systems running in data centers, which would allow companies to potentially tap into more powerful AI models without having to put all that computing power onboard.

“Any robotic application generally needs to connect the robots to some offline intelligence, whether it’s to collect data or do exception handling or whatever,” said Kashani. “It’s the connectivity piece that has to be really high performance. You need to be able to manage really unreliable networks and still reliably connect, and that’s what we solve.”

It’s also launching a data curator tool that helps companies find edge cases in the reams of real-world data a robot collects, which can then be fed back into a training model to improve performance. Its third product is a real-world, foundation-model data catalog built from Serve’s own sidewalk robots that can teach AI models how to understand complex human environments.

Kashani said he’s been thinking about this idea — a playbook he learned from Amazon — for years.

“When the technology is so nascent, you have got to build the end-to-end application because that’s the only way you know what to build, but then over time, as the technology gets more advanced, a lot more people are going to be wanting to build similar things,” he said. “And what you want to do is to open your technology so others build with you and on your platform.”

items.content:
오픈AI가 기존 모델보다 보안 취약점에 대한 공격 성공률을 51% 높인 사이버 보안 특화 AI 모델 'GPT-6 사이버(GPT-6 Cyber)'를 출시했다. 리눅스 운영체제에서 실제 작동하는 공격 코드 948건을 개발하고 파이어폭스에서 새로운 고위험 취약점 81건을 발견하는 등 보안 점검 능력을 강화했으며, 주요 보안 기업과 협력해 기업 시장 공략에도 나섰다.

오픈AI는 5일(현지시간) 공식 블로그 를 통해 GPT-6 사이버를 공개하고, 승인된 일부 보안 전문가와 기업을 대상으로 API와 '코덱스'를 통한 서비스를 시작했다고 발표했다.

GPT-6 사이버는 지난 9월 출시한 'GPT-6 아스트라'를 기반으로 취약점 발견과 공격 코드 개발, 침투 테스트 등에 특화한 모델이다. 추가 훈련을 통해 실제 공격 가능성을 검증하는 능력을 높이는 동시에, 보안 전문가가 허가받은 작업을 수행할 때 발생하는 불필요한 거부도 줄였다.

특히 취약점을 이용하는 공격 코드를 직접 작성하고 테스트 환경에서 실행하며, 실패하면 다른 방법을 시도할 수 있다. 발견한 문제에 대한 수정안도 제안한다. 기존 모델에도 이러한 기능이 있었지만, GPT-6 사이버는 실제 공격 성공률과 허가된 작업을 수행하는 능력을 크게 개선했다.

대표적인 사례가 리눅스 커널이다. 리눅스는 서버와 클라우드 인프라 등 수많은 디지털 시스템의 기반으로, 운영체제의 핵심인 커널에서 권한 상승 취약점이 발견되면 공격자가 관리자 수준의 권한을 확보하는 데 악용할 수 있다.

회사 연구진은 GPT-6 사이버를 활용해 리눅스 커널의 취약점 1724건을 재현하고, 이 가운데 948건에 대해 실제 작동하는 권한 상승 공격 코드를 개발했다. 같은 실험 환경에서 'GPT-5.6 솔'이 공격에 성공한 166건보다 5배 이상 많은 수치다. 로이터에 따르면 948건 중 588건은 이전까지 알려지지 않은 취약점이었다. 오픈AI는 중요한 보안 문제 304건을 수정안과 함께 리눅스 개발자들에게 전달했다.

모질라의 웹 브라우저 파이어폭스에서도 새로운 고위험 취약점 81건을 발견하고, 기존에 알려진 취약점 30건의 위험도가 이전 평가보다 높다는 사실을 확인했다. 취약점을 재현하는 테스트와 수정안을 제공, 모질라는 상당수 문제를 수정했다.

벤치마크에서도 성능 개선을 확인했다. 실제 취약점에 대한 공격 성공률을 측정하는 '익스플로잇짐(ExploitGym)'에서 48.5%를 기록했다. 이전 모델인 'GPT-5.6 사이버'의 32.1%보다 16.4%포인트 높아 상대적으로 51% 개선됐다. 소스 코드 없이 웹 애플리케이션의 취약점을 찾아내는 평가에서도 40.3%를 기록해 GPT-6 아스트라의 32.0%를 앞섰다.

외부 평가에서도 성능 향상이 나타났다. 보안 평가업체 이레귤러(Irregular)가 실시한 장시간 공격 작업 평가에서 11개 과제를 모두 최소 한 차례 해결했다. AI 코딩 에이전트 '데빈'을 개발한 코그니션(Cognition)은 자체 취약점 발견 및 공격 평가에서 23%를 기록해 종전 최고 점수인 13%를 넘어섰다고 밝혔다.

그러나 모든 평가에서 범용 모델을 앞선 것은 아니다. 실제 소프트웨어와 하드웨어의 취약점을 평가하는 '프론티어사이버(FrontierCyber)'에서는 288개 과제 중 90개를 해결해 GPT-6 아스트라의 96개에 미치지 못했다. 아티피셜 애널리시스 등의 독립적인 종합 성능 평가도 아직 확인되지 않았다.

오픈AI는 이번 모델을 기반으로 기업용 사이버 보안 사업도 강화하고 있다. 팔로알토 네트웍스와 시스코, 센티넬원 등 주요 보안 기업들이 GPT-6 사이버를 취약점 분석과 보안 연구에 활용하고 있다. 특히 팔로알토 네트웍스는 자사 보안 연구에 이 모델을 활용하는 동시에, '유닛42 연속 프런티어 AI 방어(Unit 42 Continuous Frontier AI Defense)' 서비스를 통해 기업 고객에게도 관련 기술을 제공하고 있다고 밝혔다.

이는 전문 모델을 직접 공급하는 데 그치지 않고 기존 보안업체의 서비스를 통해 기업 시장으로 진출하고 있다는 의미다. 팔로알토 네트웍스의 해당 서비스는 AI를 활용해 기업 시스템의 취약점을 지속적으로 발견하고 공격 가능성을 검증하며, 수정 작업까지 지원한다.

오픈AI는 사이버 보안 모델을 '데이브레이크(Daybreak)'라는 별도 서비스 체계로 운영하고 있다. 일반적인 코드 검토와 취약점 검증을 지원하는 '데이브레이크 블루(Blue)'와 실제 공격 코드 개발, 침투 테스트 등 고급 보안 작업을 지원하는 '데이브레이크 레드(Red)'로 구분된다. GPT-6 사이버는 레드 고객에게 제공하는 모델로, 이용자 신원과 작업 권한을 별도로 확인한다.

이번 모델의 사이버 보안 역량은 오픈AI 자체 안전 평가에서 최고 단계인 '심각(Critical)'으로 분류됐다. 기존 GPT-5.6 사이버의 '높음(High)'보다 한 단계 올라간 것으로, GPT-6 아스트라도 이미 같은 등급을 받은 바 있다. 이처럼 강력한 기능의 오용을 막기 위해 허가된 작업 범위를 지키는 능력도 강화했다. 관련 평가에서 99.93%의 비율로 허가 범위를 준수했으며, 추가 안전 지침을 적용했을 때는 평가 대상 전체에서 범위를 지켰다.

기술 사양은 105만토큰의 컨텍스트 창과 최대 12만8000토큰의 출력 길이를 지원하며, 텍스트와 이미지 입력을 처리할 수 있다. 기본 단문 컨텍스트 기준 API 가격은 100만토큰당 입력 20달러, 출력 100달러이며 캐시된 입력은 2달러다.

현재 서비스는 승인된 데이브레이크 레드 고객으로 제한된다. 오픈AI는 앞으로 몇주에 걸쳐 승인된 고객 전체로 제공 대상을 넓히고, 발전소와 수처리 시설 등 핵심 인프라 보안 담당자를 위한 전용 접근 그룹도 신설할 계획이다.

전문가 칼럼 입력 :2026/11/06 06:00

알고리즘은 내가 좋아하는 영화를 알고 있고 어제 본 드라마를 기억하고 다음에 보고 싶은 콘텐츠까지 귀신같이 추천한다. 그런데 우리 동네에 산불이 났을 때 어디로 대피해야 하는지, 우리 지역을 이끌 후보자가 어떤 공약을 내걸었는지는 누가 알려줄까.

지난 2022년 3월 울진·삼척 일대를 덮친 대형 산불 당시 LG헬로비전 지역채널은 15차례 뉴스특보와 130회 이상의 현장 연결을 진행했다. 산불 상황과 대응 요령은 영어와 중국어, 베트남어 자막으로도 전달됐다. 지역에 거주하는 외국인들도 재난정보에서 소외되지 않도록 하기 위해서였다.

세계적인 콘텐츠가 손안으로 쏟아지는 시대다. 그러나 위급한 순간 우리에게 필요한 것은 화제의 드라마가 아니라 집 앞의 상황을 알려주는 정보일 수 있다. 미디어의 가치는 얼마나 많은 콘텐츠를 보여주느냐뿐 아니라 누구에게 어떤 정보를 전달하느냐에 달려 있다.

지역 민주주의에서도 마찬가지다. 지난 6월 지방선거에서 케이블TV 지역채널들은 후보자 토론회와 공약 검증, 유권자 참여 프로그램을 잇달아 선보였다. CMB는 광역·기초의원 후보들의 무료 방송연설을 지원했고, JCN울산중앙방송은 후보자들에게 1분의 발언 기회를 제공했다. 전국적인 관심을 받기 어려운 지역 후보들의 목소리까지 주민들에게 전달하려는 노력이었다.

지역의 일꾼을 뽑는 선거에서 정작 우리 동네 후보가 누구인지 알기 어렵다면 그것은 민주주의의 빈틈이다. 지역채널은 그 빈틈을 메워 왔다. 전국 방송이 미처 다루지 못하는 지방의회의 결정과 골목의 문제, 주민들의 작은 목소리를 기록하는 것도 지역채널의 몫이다.

정보는 넘쳐나는데 내 삶에 필요한 정보는 부족한 시대. 정부가 제시한 '미디어 기본사회'는 바로 이러한 역설을 해소하는 데서 출발해야 한다.

미디어 기본사회는 단순히 더 많은 콘텐츠를 볼 수 있는 사회가 아니다. 어디에 살든 필요한 정보를 얻고, 나이와 경제적 형편에 관계없이 미디어를 이용하며, 새로운 기술의 혜택에서도 소외되지 않는 사회다.

이런 관점에서 케이블TV가 오랫동안 지켜온 가치들을 다시 살펴볼 필요가 있다.

대표적인 것이 보편적 방송 접근권이다. 스마트폰으로 영상을 검색하고 여러 플랫폼을 넘나드는 일이 익숙한 사람도 있지만, 누군가에게는 회원가입과 로그인부터 어려운 과정이다. 새로운 기술을 배우지 않아도 익숙한 리모컨으로 방송을 시청하고 싶은 사람도 있다.

케이블TV의 8VSB 서비스는 별도의 디지털 셋톱박스 없이 비교적 저렴한 비용으로 방송을 볼 수 있는 방식이다. 화려한 기능은 없지만 고령층과 디지털 취약계층에게는 중요한 선택지다. 케이블TV 업계가 이 서비스를 '모두의 TV'라는 공동 브랜드로 발전시키려는 이유도 여기에 있다.

인공지능 시대에는 또 다른 과제가 기다리고 있다. AI가 일상으로 들어올수록 기술을 활용하는 사람과 그렇지 못한 사람의 격차는 더 커질 수 있다. 케이블TV는 지역 복지관과 노인대학, 주민센터 등과 협력해 '우리 동네 AI 교실'을 추진할 계획이다. 주민들이 AI를 생활 속에서 안전하고 유용하게 활용하도록 돕겠다는 것이다.

지난 10월8일 케이블TV 업계는 '미디어 기본사회, 케이블TV가 잇겠습니다'라는 약속을 내놓았다. 지역의 알 권리를 지키고, 누구나 미디어를 누릴 수 있도록 하며, AI 시대에도 누구도 뒤처지지 않게 하겠다는 다짐이었다.

하지만 이 약속을 지속하려면 풀어야 할 숙제가 있다.

케이블TV의 방송 수익은 감소하고 지역채널 제작 여건은 갈수록 어려워지고 있다. 재난이 발생하면 현장으로 달려가야 하고, 선거 때마다 후보자와 유권자의 목소리를 담아야 하지만 이러한 공적 역할을 안정적으로 뒷받침할 제도적 기반은 충분하지 않다.

이제 지역채널의 법적 위상을 분명히 하고 공적 역할에 걸맞은 지원체계를 마련해야 한다. 유료방송 시장의 변화에 맞지 않는 규제와 부담구조도 합리적으로 개선할 필요가 있다. 케이블TV의 지속가능성은 특정 산업의 생존을 넘어 지역 주민의 알 권리와 미디어 접근권을 지키는 문제이기 때문이다.

미디어 기본사회는 선언이 아니라 국민의 일상에서 확인되어야 한다. 산불 현장에서 대피정보를 전하고, 지역 후보자의 목소리를 알리고, 기술에 익숙하지 않은 어르신이 불편 없이 방송을 보는 것. 거창하지 않지만 바로 이런 일들이 미디어 기본사회의 출발점이다.

알고리즘은 수많은 콘텐츠 가운데 내가 좋아할 만한 이야기를 찾아준다. 그러나 우리 동네에서 반드시 전해야 할 이야기는 누군가 직접 찾아 나서야 한다.

세상을 연결하는 기술은 많다. 우리 동네를 잇는 방송도 있어야 한다.

items.title: Inside GitHub’s new Git storage architecture
items.summary: GitHub's new Git storage architecture is built so thousands of agents can push to a single repository at once. Here's how it works. The post Inside GitHub’s new Git storage architecture appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
items.content:
Last week at GitHub Universe, we announced our new Git storage architecture, capable of handling thousands of writes per second with reads that scale on demand. Through internal testing, we’ve demonstrated the ability to support 5,000 concurrent agents working on a repository, sending 7,200 pushes per second to a repo, all while serving read traffic with consistently low latency. This new architecture is the foundation for GitHub to support agentic development for hundreds of millions of developers, and we’ve been building it underneath GitHub while it keeps running.

Over the past year, agents changed what a busy repository looks like on GitHub. In our first post in this series, we laid out the two principles behind our next-generation Git storage architecture: minimize coordination, and decouple storage from compute. In our last post , we covered the bridge: moving 99.99999% of repositories into Azure, scoping the write quorum to individual references, and standing up virtual replicas backed by Azure Blob Storage.

We also left off with an observation: very little of a write needs to be ordered. Git objects are immutable and named by their contents, meaning two writers can store them at the same time without agreeing on anything. The part of a push that needs agreement is the reference update, and a reference update is tiny in comparison. Virtual replicas were the first step toward building around that, and the means by which we onboard repositories to the new architecture.

The rest of the architecture builds on that observation. Only reference updates need agreement. That lets the parts of Git infrastructure that used to be tightly coupled (storing data, serving requests, and maintaining repositories) scale independently. For developers, Git stays Git: they push, fetch, and branch the same way, with the same protections in place. Below, we walk through the requirements behind the design, follow a request through the system, and dive deep into two of its components.

We think about the scale of the GitHub platform along two axes:

Today, the busiest repositories on GitHub.com receive at most dozens of writes in a single second, typically in short bursts. As more of that work shifts to agents running in parallel and around the clock, we expect those bursts to become a sustained rate within the next year. Each push leads to more reads: CI runs, deployment systems pull the new commit, and other agents fetch it for context. This read fan-out results in a large amplification effect on overall traffic that scales with writes.

We’re already seeing this trend play out on repositories at the top of the curve. The chart below shows daily requests to one repository on GitHub from March to May, when its traffic grew about 4x. Its growth has continued on an exponential trajectory since then.

We have to plan for a world where agent-driven development keeps accelerating at this speed. Instead of planning for the next increment, we set a target of at least two orders of magnitude more scale. For a single repository, that meant the new architecture needed to:

On top of that, the system had to be able to improve overall reliability and scale globally.

In May of 2026, hot on the heels of the initial Azure migration, we started working on a design that could meet those demands. We tried several approaches. In all of them, pack data lived in Azure Blob Storage, and in some we experimented with keeping reference state there too. We’ll cover some of the trade-offs we found below, but we settled on a design we felt maximized throughput while preserving the correctness, durability, availability, and latency guarantees a platform like GitHub requires. We called it “Rubicon,” a nod to the point of no return the industry crossed with agentic development.

Let’s walk through Rubicon from the top down. Many things stay the same: requests from Git clients, the API, and the web UI arrive at Spokes, which still handles routing and load balancing, and serves the internal API that the rest of GitHub uses to read and write repository data. Spokes also maintains its role as a placement and balancing service, maintaining the partitioning, isolation, and tenant fairness required for horizontal scale. The data plane underneath Spokes, in contrast, is new.

Spokes routes each request to one of a small group of virtual replicas assigned to that repository. Virtual replicas are a single fleet of disposable compute that serves reads, writes, or both. A virtual replica’s local disk is a cache that can be rebuilt at any time.

Spokes routes a repository’s traffic to the same virtual replicas when it can, which keeps their caches warm and latency low, but nothing about correctness depends on a request landing on any particular virtual replica. When a virtual replica goes away, the repository’s other virtual replicas keep serving, and a replacement fills its cache as traffic arrives.

When a repository gets busy, we add more virtual replicas. Separately, a fleet of compaction nodes works in the background, directly against Blob Storage and Ref-CAS, to merge each repository’s packs and remove unreachable objects. That work never runs on a virtual replica, meaning their CPU and memory can be almost entirely dedicated to serving requests.

There are many distinct approaches we’ve taken within the new architecture, from the software stack on the virtual replicas to how traffic routing and workload scheduling are tuned for different use cases (e.g., many small repos vs. one large one). Let’s dive deep into two components of the architecture and tell their stories centered on the two design principles.

items.title: Software squeezes more data out of Webb Telescope for imaging exoplanets
items.summary: Software optimizes a physical model of the telescope to reduce noise.
items.content:
With a huge and still-growing catalog of exoplanets, researchers are eager to take the next steps: trying to infer what conditions are like on them, either by imaging them directly or by capturing the light that has passed through their atmosphere. Both are substantial challenges, given the presence of stars that are far, far brighter than light that has come to us via the planet.

While telescopes can be fitted with devices called coronagraphs that block out much of a star’s light, there are limits to their effectiveness, caused by noise from subtle variations in the telescope’s configuration and pointing between observations. Now, researchers have developed a new software package that optimizes a physical model of the telescope in a way that allows us to better model these differences, producing low-noise imaging of exoplanets.

Central to this work is the concept of a point spread function. If you use a telescope to image a single point of light, it will not appear that way in the actual image. Instead, it will be slightly blurry and spread out, due to imperfections in the telescope hardware and the limits of our ability to keep it pointed accurately through the time it takes to image something. The mathematical description of how a telescope distorts a point of light is called its point spread function.

There are two ways to figure out what the point spread function is. One is to use the telescope to image a known target and use those observations to derive a mathematical description of the point spread function. This is effective at reducing noise but has its limits, as the behavior of the telescope hardware can change over time, and the point spread function may vary with the wavelengths being imaged.

The alternative is to try to model the hardware’s behavior and use that model to derive a point spread function. But modern telescopes are incredibly complicated instruments, with many, many factors feeding into their performance in ways that can be difficult to ascertain, even with the full engineering schematics. As a result, these models simply contain too many parameters that need to be tuned to make this route computationally tractable.

But anyone paying attention to the world of AI developments will recognize that we’ve become quite successful at tuning billions of parameters in neural networks, in part through a mathematical technique called gradient descent. And, because this is central to training large neural networks, people have put a lot of work into optimizing the performance of gradient descent on GPUs.

So a team of researchers has developed a process they’re calling FLIP (a non-acronym for Physics-based Learning for Imaging Planets) that uses a physical model of the hardware (in this case, the NIRCam on the James Webb Space Telescope) with 10 6 possible parameters, and then uses software to optimize all its parameters. The optimization starts with a simulated point spread function, then uses gradient descent to optimize its performance on data from an actual star. Run on a current GPU, this process only takes a bit more than half an hour.

The researchers then fine-tune the results on the actual scientific image they are analyzing. This last part of the process is critical, since some variables will differ between observations.

To test how this works, the researchers used observations of two stars with known exoplanets (HIP 65426 and 51 Eridani), along with a third (TYC 5899) that doesn’t have any known exoplanets but is known to vary a lot between observations. These are young stars, and two of them have massive planets that are still warm from their gravitational collapse, allowing them to have been imaged previously.

Using Webb data, the team used FLIP to boost the signal-to-noise ratio by a factor of 1.5 to 2, depending on the observations. At a wavelength that can be used to detect carbon dioxide, they were able to spot one of the planets in the Webb data for the first time. For TYC 5899, the approach boosted the sensitivity of the observations by a factor of 15.

The researchers point out that the applications go beyond getting a better view of known planets. By lowering the noise, it should also be possible to spot dimmer (and hence older or lower-mass) ones that had previously eluded detection. They also think they can modify FLIP to highlight where it’s making the most dramatic changes to the model, which can potentially tell us useful things about what’s going on with the telescope’s hardware.

items.title: Meta says US users can now video chat with their Muse AI avatar
items.summary: Meta's AI agent can now take calls as a customizable animated avatar, ahead of the launch of a Tamagotchi-like wearable designed to bring Muse to life.
items.content:
Muse Voice, a feature that lets users call and video chat with Meta’s consumer AI agent, Muse, is now available to everyone in the U.S., the company announced on Thursday.

First introduced at Meta’s Connect developer conference in September, the video-chatting feature involves new AI models, Muse Realtime Avatar and Muse Realtime Voice technology, which help power the digital avatar that chats with the user.

While other AI competitors offer voice chat features, Meta’s Muse offers a cute, animated avatar (nicknamed Jolly), which users interact with as they ask questions or request tasks to be handled on their behalf. Users can also customize the avatar as they choose, changing it to something that looks more like a person, animal, or some other character.

The company believes that anthropomorphizing Muse in this way could make consumers feel more connected to their AI agent — a connection that could grow even stronger as they begin to engage in live conversations with it.

As the Muse avatar speaks, Meta says it will use “subtle expressions and gestures” that match the tone of the conversation.

The news of the rollout was announced via blog post and on X by Meta’s chief AI officer, Alexandr Wang, who shared a demo of his Muse in action. The video saw Wang joking around, referencing his love of posting memes on X, which he told his Muse may have gotten him in trouble with his boss. His Muse, a fluffy white dog, responds with a suggestion to add disclaimers to those memes that could be misinterpreted as Meta endorsing anything risqué. (Ha!)

The added support for video chats and calls comes just before Meta’s plan to launch a Tamagotchi-like wearable device for its Muse AI agent before year-end. When the device arrives, the digital avatar will appear on its small screen, letting users talk to the agent, which can then reply or carry out tasks for them.

Meta says the real-time conversations are supported on mobile, web, and Mac and will later come to its AI Glasses and the upcoming “Muse Charm” hardware device.

items.title: Meta warns that election backlash against data centers could make AI expansion harder
items.summary: Meta warns that growing political opposition to data centers could threaten future AI investments, as communities push back against massive infrastructure projects.
items.content:
Meta president Dina Powell McCormick said that the Democratic wins in the midterm elections are going to make it a lot harder for companies to build data centers, adding that the industry has “not done as good a job as we needed to explain the benefits of these investments.”

Speaking at the WSJ Tech conference on Wednesday, the Meta exec pointed out that the backlash against data centers — which was very much on the ballot during this election season — was also tied to people’s feelings about AI technology overall.

“The visible sort of manifestation of AI is a data center, and it’s something that people can say, ‘I don’t want this in my community,’” she explained. “I think there’s an underlying bigger issue, which is how people feel about AI in general.”

Meta believes it could turn around the negative consumer sentiment around AI if it’s able to demonstrate the value, not only of the data centers coming to local communities, but also in the technology itself.

“The stakes of who builds the technology that cures cancer, that gives access to education, that is also a very fundamental difference … Mark [Zuckerberg, Meta CEO] is very ‘long human,’ and he’s betting on humans more than machines,” Powell McCormick explained. “And that’s what we mean when we say the future is for everyone. That people should not be left behind. But the way to ensure that is that this technology is democratized, that people have access to it in a very fair and transparent way,” she said.

The exec also touted Meta’s experience in building data centers, saying that the company has been doing so for 20 years, as it takes a lot of compute power to offer the products it does in the social networking space. Today, the company has data centers in 23 states, she said, and five of them, including one in Texas, are planned as projects of 1 gigawatt or more.

But Meta is now worried that it could lose some of its investments after politicians ran on anti-data-center platforms during the midterms.

“I think it’s going to be harder,” Powell McCormick said, describing what the future of building data centers looks like. “It has been hard, I should say, but I also think that it’s becoming clear what models work, and the states want those models that work.”

Specifically, communities only want data centers when it benefits them in some way, she explained, laying out the approach that Meta today uses to close its data center deals in local communities.

Successful projects see Meta paying for its own electricity, directing any tax surpluses as a result of the data centers toward teachers and first responders, keeping the labor force local, and getting bipartisan support for the project, among other things.

Going forward, she expects data center projects to come under more review and be weighed against whether the constituents actually want them.

Meta has pinned its hopes on its AI investments, particularly its consumer AI agent Muse scaling far beyond the 10 million users it has today, to become a business that one day serves billions. But even if that’s not the case, it believes that its investments in data centers will not be for nothing, as the compute itself will be valuable.

“We’re getting calls every day to lease that compute [we’ve built], and so one way or another, we’re seeing a path to monetization,” Powell McCormick said.

items.title: OpenAI released a new cybersecurity model. Is that enough?
items.summary: OpenAI's newest cybersecurity model comes out as AI labs face scrutiny of their work to protect digital infrastructure.
items.content:
Max Justicz, the chief technology officer and co-founder of the startup Charge Robotics, used an OpenAI model to find a severe vulnerability that — if exploited — could allow hackers to take control of servers running Ubuntu, a widely used open source Linux-based operating system.

Justicz, who has a hobbyist’s interest in cybersecurity and previously found a vulnerability in the same codebase, told TechCrunch that he found this issue using GPT 5.6 Sol, released in July, through the AI maker’s Daybreak Blue, a program that gives cybersecurity defenders access to powerful frontier models.

“I literally just aimed ChatGPT at the same body of code and said ‘I found this bug previously that was fixed several years ago, please find bugs as bad or worse,’ and it came back in two hours with this,” Justicz said. “It’s extremely convoluted and hard for a human to find, but it works!”

He reported the issue to the Debian Project, which maintains the software in question and issued a patch to fix the vulnerability. There has been no known evidence of exploitation. Still, the ease with which he found it suggests that we’ve only seen the tip of the iceberg when it comes to potential exploits that even novice hackers can utilize with the help of AI models.

“I can only imagine what one could do with more time and access to less neutered models. We should expect some extremely crazy bugs to be found and exploited over the next few months,” Justicz wrote in a social media thread discussing his finding. “This might be obvious to most folks here, but there is currently huge alpha in taking some code or binary someone has not audited yet and just aiming a powerful AI model at it.”

OpenAI appears to have noticed. Today, the AI giant announced a new model focused on cybersecurity, ChatGPT Cyber, would be made available to the highest tier of users in the cybersecurity program, Daybreak Red, which allows offensive cybersecurity researchers tools for vulnerability hunting and development. Yesterday, OpenAI said that the same model had been used to scan and prepare patches for vulnerabilities in the Linux kernel, finding 948 potential issues. OpenAI also found 81 “novel” vulnerabilities in Firefox, the web browser.

“Our goal is to dramatically expand Daybreak, bringing advanced security research to organizations of every size, independent researchers, and open-source maintainers,” the frontier lab said in a statement.

OpenAI has insisted that there is a narrow window of time for the people who safeguard digital infrastructure to take action before AI models become even better at hacking and easier to access. For cyber defenders, however, it can feel like the frontier labs have unleashed a mountain of new work that outstrips their resources. Justicz said that he personally spent about $5,000 on subscriptions and tokens to find several exploits.

Besides Daybreak’s model access, OpenAI has also announced a $1 billion initiative to support cybersecurity professionals in the program who work on critical infrastructure like the electrical grid or water systems.

The Daybreak program has its own critiques. Justicz notes that the frontier lab appears to have recently “nerfed” Daybreak Blue to make it less useful at finding vulnerabilities. On one hand, it may be good to limit access from potential bad actors — Justicz said he just uploaded a photo of his driver’s license to join the program. On the other, cybersecurity professionals say they have one hand tied if they can’t use frontier technology while bad actors can deploy open-weight models with abliterated guardrails .

Still, OpenAI says just “thousands” of cybersecurity professionals are participating in the Daybreak program, versus a far larger number of potential hackers.

It’s unclear if frontier labs are devoting enough of their resources to this issue. Eric Wallace, a researcher on OpenAI’s technical staff, said that “we are now allocating a significant amount of our frontier compute towards discovering and patching vulnerabilities in open source codebases, fully pro bono.”

But the Linux bug hunt cost $1.2 million, which is significantly less than the approximate $6 million token spend the company invested in finding a potential solution to a famous problem of fluid dynamics.

If there is a narrow window of time to patch the digital infrastructure the world depends on, more urgency may be required.

items.content:
Muse AI agent now has voices and ‘expressive’ avatars that animate while chatting with you.

Meta now lets you have voice conversations with your Muse AI agent in real time, CEO Mark Zuckerberg announced today .

The feature has been rolled out to me, and I gave it a spin on the iOS app while writing this article. As you chat with your Muse agent, the avatar at the top of your conversation animates in time with the words that it’s saying. You can also change the tone of the voice by just asking your agent about what you want and letting it decide or by browsing through a bunch of options in the avatar settings.

In my brief tests, my Muse agent responds quickly over voice, though it occasionally pauses while it’s looking up information or checking something for me (like it would with a text chat query). It also animates what it’s saying well, though for my particular avatar, it’s been a little uncanny. I set my Muse agent’s avatar to look like Mark Zuckerberg as a constant reminder that I’m chatting with a Meta service (I refuse to be charmed by a Jolly! ), and seeing the digital Zuckerberg facsimile actually talk with me is quite weird. I also can’t get my Muse agent’s voice to sound exactly like Mark Zuckerberg.

Muse’s voice mode and expressive avatars are rolling out now in the US for the app, Meta says . They’re coming “soon” for Meta’s AI glasses and will also be available for its forthcoming Muse Charm gadget , which is supposed to ship this year.
